subject: Nimbus Financial — incident briefing, findings, and remediation timeline
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@nimbusfin.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Unexpected inference discrepancies after midday deployment

Hi Irene,

We started seeing inconsistent outputs from the Redwood inference endpoint for our 'statement-summary' route around 11:40am ET today. The issues appeared as:
- Shortened summaries (missing last-paragraph) for ~12% of requests
- Occasional 502 responses for otherwise identical payloads

This is impacting our reconciliation flow; we can reproduce with a small sample set and have attached two examples. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (model rollout, config, or patching)?

Sample evidence attached: request-20280629-1142.json, request-20280629-1143.json

Thanks,
Alex
Product Ops | Nimbus Financial

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -0400
Subject: Preliminary findings and immediate mitigations (Nimbus incident)

Alex — short update after our first pass of the traces and logs. Thank you for the quick samples; they were very helpful.

Preliminary findings (summary):
- Timeline highlights:
  • 2028-06-28 20:47 UTC — internal canary model rollout to serve 'statement-summary' variants (automated job).
  • 2028-06-29 02:12 UTC — a subset of API nodes reported elevated cache miss rates; an eviction job did not complete on those nodes.
  • 2028-06-29 03:10 UTC — increased 502s and truncated outputs observed on affected nodes.
- Root cause (prelim): an interaction between our model-variant rollout and the prefix/KV cache eviction process caused stale keys to remain on a minority of serving nodes. Requests routed to those nodes received outputs inconsistent with the active model variant.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back the recent canary to the previous model distribution for the impacted route (completed 2028-06-29 04:05 UTC).
- Invalidated and rebuilt KV/prefix cache on all serving nodes (completed 2028-06-29 05:00 UTC).
- Deployed a targeted hotfix to make cache eviction idempotent in the face of paused background jobs (patch v1).

Customer impact: we estimate ~0.8% of total requests between 02:10–05:00 UTC returned truncated or 502s for your tenant. We will share a detailed timeline and corrective plan in the full RCA.

Attachments: nimbus_prelim_logs_20280629.zip (logs for the affected nodes)

Action items in-flight (short):
- OPS-7821: hard invalidate caches on the legacy pool (Markus, ETA 2028-06-29 05:00 UTC)
- CS-405: customer notification + offer of remediation credits (Grace, ETA 2028-06-30 COB)

I'll follow up with the complete RCA and a remediation schedule by EOD tomorrow. Please tell me if you need earlier remediation or a call.

— Irene

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 12:45:00 -0400
Subject: Final RCA and remediation timeline — Nimbus incident (June 29)

Alex, Markus, Grace — final RCA attached. Thank you for your patience; we know this impacted critical reconciliation runs and we appreciate the collaboration during triage.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
A canary model rollout performed late on 2028-06-28 interacted with a paused/failed background cache eviction job on a subset of inference nodes. The result: stale KV/prefix cache entries persisted and caused inconsistent tokenization/backoff behavior for certain sequences, producing truncated outputs and intermittent 502 responses for a small fraction of requests. We have completed rollback, cache rebuild, and a hotfix; additional guardrails are scheduled to prevent recurrence.

Detailed timeline (select entries):
- 2028-06-28 20:47 UTC — Canary rollout initiated (model v2-canary).
- 2028-06-29 02:12 UTC — Node pool A reports eviction job failure due to resource throttling.
- 2028-06-29 03:10 UTC — Monitoring alerts: error rate spike on /v1/generate for statement-summary route.
- 2028-06-29 03:25 UTC — We began routing traffic away from Node pool A as a mitigation.
- 2028-06-29 04:05 UTC — Canary rolled back to v2-stable.
- 2028-06-29 05:00 UTC — Cache rebuilt and validation checks completed.

Root cause analysis (concise):
- Primary cause: race between canary model rollout and a non-idempotent cache eviction workflow that failed under resource contention.
- Contributing factors: insufficient pre-rollout validation for background evictions and lack of a cross-node cache-coordination check.

Remediation and commitments (owners and due dates):
- Make eviction workflow idempotent and add retry/backoff logic (Markus Klein, ETA 2028-07-15).
- Add pre-rollout validation to ensure background maintenance jobs are healthy before canary starts (Markus Klein, ETA 2028-07-08).
- Implement cross-node cache-consistency checker and an automated reconcile job (Engineering, ETA 2028-07-22).
- Update customer-facing incident runbook to include immediate rollback criteria and quicker CS notifications (Grace O'Connor, ETA 2028-07-05).
- Offer remediation credit equivalent to two days of usage for affected windows (Grace O'Connor / Billing, ETA 2028-07-03).

What we verified post-fix:
- End-to-end integration tests covering canary + cache eviction scenarios were added and passed in staging.
- We replayed representative request samples from your tenant across the repaired pool — no truncated outputs or elevated 502s observed.

Attachments: nimbus_redwood_rca_20280630.pdf, playbook_hotfix_patch_v1.diff
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-nimbus-rca-20280630, https://jira.redwood.com/browse/OPS-7821

If you'd like a 30-minute walk-through of the RCA with our engineering leads, we're available Wednesday or Thursday morning ET — what works best for you?

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this as a priority and will follow up with progress updates on the remediation items above.

— Irene Choi
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
